name: Claraveil
description: Claraveil is a transparent aligned-SWCNT thin-film material produced by Apex Nanofabrication through a vacuum filtration and transfer process that creates optically clear sheets with 97% light transmission across the visible spectrum. The CNT network provides electrical conductivity throughout the transparent layer, making it the dominant material for touch-sensitive displays, electrochromic windows, and flexible screen substrates — replacing indium tin oxide in virtually every premium display application. Claraveil sheets can be produced down to 50-nanometer thickness while remaining handleable and electrically functional.
story_hooks: Claraveil's conductivity means every display built with it is technically capable of transmitting data — a hardware exploit allows certain Claraveil-based screens to be remotely activated as surveillance sensors.
A Veilweave Textiles fashion line incorporates Claraveil panels as wearable displays — but the supply chain for the film runs through a single fabrication facility that is now under threat.
Someone has developed a method to print hidden circuitry into Claraveil sheets during manufacture — screens shipped to corporate clients contain invisible data-exfiltration hardware.
